finding.title: OS Command Injection
finding.trigger: An attacker can inject malicious commands into the 'url' parameter.
finding.assumptions: The 'url' parameter is attacker-controlled and can contain arbitrary input.

parsed.refutation_attempt: Checked for constant arguments and unreachable paths. The 'url' parameter is concatenated with the 'executable' string, which is set based on the platform. However, the 'executable' string is not derived from user input and is hardcoded for each platform. Therefore, the 'url' parameter is not directly used to construct the command without any checks or sanitization.

finding.title: Improper Neutralization of Argument Delimiters
finding.trigger: An attacker can inject special characters into the 'url' parameter to alter the command structure.
finding.assumptions: The 'url' parameter is attacker-controlled and can contain arbitrary input.

parsed.refutation_attempt: Checked for constant arguments and unreachable paths. The 'url' parameter is concatenated with the 'executable' string, which is determined by preprocessor directives based on the platform. The 'executable' string is not attacker-controlled and is hardcoded for each platform. Therefore, the 'url' parameter is only used as an argument to the system command and does not alter the command structure itself. The code does not provide a way for an attacker to inject special characters that would alter the command structure.
